scope: Canonical WPAWS 11.1.7 UI, 17 agent roles, prompts, chains, browser memory, exports, file handling, public worker adapter, proactive research mandate, capability claims and Human Gate controls.
strengths: Canonical UI identifies 17 specialised roles and a Human-governed institutional context.
Server-side WPA worker routing exists for primary AI calls.
WPAWS is already connected to broader WPA public-source and scholarly architecture.
Document-first review/editor/integrity roles exist and can be strengthened without rebuilding the entire UI.

findings.title: Silent long-prompt truncation
findings.evidence: Browser runtime truncates prompts near 690 characters and worker /ask validates a 700-character maximum.
findings.risk: Books, long reviews, manuscripts and integrity checks can appear complete while only a prefix reaches the backend.
findings.remediation: Disable silent truncation; preflight and block over-limit prompts. Build a separately protected Long Document Adapter before claiming long-document coverage.

findings.title: Legacy browser provider-key storage and contradictory privacy copy
findings.evidence: API keys are stored in localStorage and a legacy direct Anthropic web-search path exists while the modal states keys are never sent externally.
findings.risk: Credential exposure and misleading security expectations.
findings.remediation: Remove browser key use/storage; route provider calls server-side only; repurpose key UI as server-adapter status.

findings.title: Academic-integrity capability overclaim
findings.evidence: Plagiarism UI offers all databases, Scholar/JSTOR and COBISS+WPA while the actual prompt is document-first; output asks for estimated originality percentage.
findings.risk: False precision and false database-coverage impression.
findings.remediation: Convert to Academic Integrity Guardian; document-only coverage by default; no originality percentage; disable unverified database choices; Human Gate for conclusions.

findings.title: Citation fabrication risk
findings.evidence: Canonical citation workflow can request 10-15 bibliography records without requiring verified source retrieval.
findings.risk: Hallucinated academic references can enter manuscripts.
findings.remediation: Never invent finished citations; unverified items must be labelled candidates and verified before publication.

findings.title: Automatic chain is sequential but not truly context-linked
findings.evidence: startChain invokes agents in order but does not reliably pass one result as the next agent input.
findings.risk: UI implies an integrated workflow while steps may work on unrelated/default form state.
findings.remediation: Pass explicit chain context, label excerpts as partial under the current adapter limit, and stop the chain on adapter/Human Gate failures.

findings.title: Hybrid mode appends rather than reconciles
findings.evidence: Second model output is appended below the first as polishing.
findings.risk: Duplicates, contradictions and false impression of consensus.
findings.remediation: Run two independent analyses and present them separately for Human Gate comparison; do not auto-merge.

findings.title: Version and runtime drift
findings.evidence: Canonical page contains legacy WPAWS 9.0/16-agent engine constants alongside WPAWS 11.1.7/17-agent code; app.js is explicitly legacy non-canonical.
findings.risk: Duplicate function definitions, stale model labels and unclear single source of truth.
findings.remediation: Use governed external runtime overlay now; progressively remove inline legacy engine blocks and centralise agent definitions/capabilities.

findings.title: Local mode is a demo, not a local AI engine
findings.evidence: Local buttons exist but the main execution path has no true local-model call.
findings.remediation: Rename to Local Preview and explicitly state no external AI model ran; keep local integrity heuristic as document-only preview.

findings.title: Export format mismatch
findings.evidence: docx/pdf selections currently produce text/plain and mostly .md naming.
findings.remediation: TXT/Markdown as real text formats, Word/RTF as actual RTF, PDF as print-to-PDF flow until a real PDF generator is integrated.

findings.title: Unsafe HTML sinks in history/file UI
findings.evidence: History preview and uploaded file names are interpolated into innerHTML; toast also accepts unsanitised message HTML.
findings.risk: DOM XSS from adversarial model text, errors or filenames.
findings.remediation: Use DOM creation/textContent and escaped formatting.

findings.title: PDF extraction is heuristic and silent
findings.evidence: Browser code scans raw PDF binary text operators and stores a 12,000-character preview.
findings.risk: Incomplete/garbled document analysis presented as representative.
findings.remediation: Mark PDF extraction experimental and preview-only; expose truncation; require a verified parser for production long-document analysis.

findings.title: Persistent browser memory lacks explicit retention/privacy controls
findings.evidence: Generated documents are stored in localStorage under wpaws_memory_v9.
findings.risk: Sensitive content can remain on a shared device.
findings.remediation: Add 30-day retention, local-only disclosure, no-sensitive-data warning and manual clear path.

findings.title: Provider status is inferred from keys/labels rather than health
findings.evidence: UI status historically reflects local key presence and hard-coded provider/model names.
findings.risk: A configured-looking provider can be unavailable or routed differently.
findings.remediation: Use server health endpoint; treat model names as routing preferences, not guaranteed deployed model versions.

findings.title: Worker CORS is not authentication
findings.evidence: Server-side callers can omit Origin; the public /ask endpoint is therefore not protected merely by browser CORS.
findings.risk: Potential provider-cost abuse if expensive capabilities or long payloads are exposed publicly.
findings.remediation: Keep public short-message limit; protect future long-document/provider-intensive endpoints with explicit abuse controls such as authentication/Turnstile/rate limits and server-side quotas.

findings.title: Agent prompt quality is uneven
findings.evidence: Some roles enforce anti-hallucination rules while others request confident or fabricated-looking outputs such as an obligatory quote or rigid scoring.
findings.remediation: Apply a common governance contract and strengthen all 17 agent prompts.

findings.title: i18n duplication
findings.evidence: Large inline translation dictionaries coexist with external locale files and shared translator runtime.
findings.remediation: Move toward locale files as the single source of truth after hardening stabilises.

findings.title: Accessibility state can be strengthened
findings.evidence: Generated output regions and some dynamic controls lack consistent live-region semantics.
findings.remediation: Mark result boxes aria-live, use real buttons/textContent for dynamic items, add descriptive capability titles.

release_gates: No originality percentage without an auditable corpus/method
No long-document production claim until protected adapter is tested
No provider-active claim without runtime health evidence
No external publication or doctrine change without Human Gate
